system_description.narrative_title: Trump–Xi summit: trade truce and tech rivalry amid pageantry
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is the high‑profile Trump–Xi summit that extended a US–China trade truce while foregrounding competition over AI, semiconductors, autos, rare earths and Taiwan. The visit combined ceremonial pageantry with limited immediate policy breakthroughs, producing short‑term cooling of tariff/hostility risks but raising medium‑term questions about supply‑chain resilience, export controls, allied reactions and technological decoupling. Domestic politics on both sides, allied security concerns and corporate exposure shape feedbacks that may either reinforce détente or accelerate bifurcation.
system_description.scope: Bilateral US–China political and economic interactions during the summit window: trade truce negotiations and extensions; AI and semiconductor dialogues; export controls and supply‑chain flows (autos, rare earths, datacenter tech); Taiwan and regional security flashpoints; allied and legislative responses (US Congress, EU/UK policy); major corporate stakeholders and market reactions.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical‑economic order (international trade and security architecture, global supply chains and multilateral governance framed around US–China strategic competition).
adjacent_subsystems: East Asian security arena (Taiwan, South China Sea, regional militaries and diplomacy)
Global technology and semiconductor ecosystem (AI chips, data‑center hardware, export controls)
Automotive and manufacturing supply chains (Chinese auto expansion in Europe, vehicle bans)
European and allied trade‑policy coordination (EU/UK tariff strategy, allied pressures)

variables.name: Bilateral political tension
variables.description: The overall level of political strain and adversarial interaction between the two governments as perceived in diplomatic, trade and security arenas.

variables.name: Trade barrier intensity
variables.description: The aggregate severity and prevalence of tariffs, quotas, sanctions and other trade-restricting measures affecting cross-border goods and services.

variables.name: Degree of technological decoupling
variables.description: The extent to which technology ecosystems (standards, supply chains, R&D collaboration and product interoperability) are diverging between the two sides.

variables.name: Supply‑chain resilience
variables.description: The capacity of critical cross-border supply chains to absorb shocks, re-route, and maintain flows of components and finished goods.

variables.name: Export control strictness
variables.description: The rigor and scope of policies restricting the export of sensitive technologies, components and dual‑use items to counterpart markets.

variables.name: Allied policy alignment
variables.description: The degree of convergence or divergence among third-party governments' policies and actions in response to the bilateral interaction.

variables.name: Corporate market exposure
variables.description: The aggregate economic exposure of firms (supply, sales, investment) to the counterpart economy and linked markets.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure
variables.description: The intensity of public opinion, interest-group lobbying and legislative momentum within each polity that shapes foreign‑economic decisions.

variables.name: Diplomatic signaling flow
variables.description: The rate and prominence of official symbolic actions, visits, statements and rituals used to convey intentions and manage optics.

variables.name: Capital and investment flows
variables.description: The volume and direction of cross-border portfolio, M&A and greenfield investment movements between the economies and linked markets.

variables.name: Technology capability gap
variables.description: The measurable difference in advanced technological capabilities, such as semiconductor design/fabrication and AI systems, between actors in the system.

variables.name: Semiconductor supply concentration
variables.description: The degree to which critical semiconductor inputs, manufacturing capacity and vendor sources are concentrated within limited producers or regions.

variables.name: Rare‑earths supply concentration
variables.description: The extent to which extraction, processing and export capacity for rare‑earth elements is concentrated and therefore susceptible to disruption or leverage.

variables.name: Security flashpoint risk
variables.description: The probability and potential intensity of military or coercive incidents emerging in contested regions or domains that could escalate bilateral tensions.

variables.name: Legislative action pressure
variables.description: The tempo and intensity of legislative proposals, restrictions and oversight actions targeting economic or technology links between parties.

variables.name: Multilateral governance effectiveness
variables.description: The capacity of international institutions and cooperative frameworks to mediate disputes, set norms and manage shared cross‑border problems.

catalysts.title: U.S.-China trade truce extended through January
catalysts.description: The bilateral trade truce announced at the summit is formally extended into January, preserving tariff/negotiation moratoria and deferring new trade measures.
catalysts.rationale: "U.S.-China trade truce extended for two months..." and "extend trade truce to January"—keeps moratorium on new measures, shapes optics.

catalysts.title: Planned Trump visit to China in November
catalysts.description: Trump's announced meeting with Xi in China in November is a scheduled high‑visibility bilateral visit likely to generate major diplomatic signaling.
catalysts.rationale: "Trump says he will meet Xi in China in November"—a scheduled summit that will drive diplomatic signals and optics.

catalysts.title: USTR to release trade-negotiation details
catalysts.description: USTR indicated detailed information on U.S.-China trade negotiations will be published on the coming Monday, clarifying near‑term bargaining posture.
catalysts.rationale: "Details on U.S.-China trade negotiations coming Monday, USTR Greer says"—official disclosure can shift barrier expectations and signals.

catalysts.title: Senate push to ban Chinese cars
catalysts.description: Senators are seeking quick approval or debate of a permanent US ban on Chinese cars, creating immediate legislative pressure on auto trade links.
catalysts.rationale: "Lawmakers to seek Senate approval of permanent US ban on Chinese cars" and "US senators press for quick Chinese vehicle ban this week"—legislative momentum.

catalysts.title: Ongoing U.S.-China AI dialogue
catalysts.description: Initial AI talks and summit-level conversations signal a continuing bilateral AI dialogue that could shape cooperation, norms and controls in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: "China confirms first AI talks with U.S. have taken place" and "AI safety talks on the table"—dialogue likely to continue shaping tech links.

catalysts.title: Risk of Chinese rare‑earths export curbs
catalysts.description: Headlines flag China's dominance in rare earths and prior yttrium curbs, raising the prospect Beijing could use export restrictions as leverage in months ahead.
catalysts.rationale: "China's rare earths dominance to overshadow Trump's talks" and "US, Japanese officials discussed China's yttrium curbs"—export curbs risk.

catalysts.title: U.S. moves to keep Chinese datacentre tech out of sensitive systems
catalysts.description: Legislative and regulatory efforts to exclude Chinese data‑centre hardware and networking gear from sensitive U.S. systems are advancing, potentially broadening tech restrictions.
catalysts.rationale: "US lawmakers aim to keep China's datacenter tech out of sensitive government systems" and "China reviews dependence on Broadcom switches"—policy moves to restrict tech links.

catalysts.title: US-China coordination around APEC/G20 hosting
catalysts.description: Leaders agreed to support each other in hosting APEC and G20 summits, creating focused cooperation and signaling opportunities around upcoming multilateral meetings.
catalysts.rationale: "Trump and Xi agreed to support each other in hosting APEC, G20 summits"—shapes multilateral agenda and optics.
